correctness.rationale: For primes p=5 mod8 with ord_p(2)=p-1, r=(p-5)/2 is divisible by four. The ternary last columns L2=(10)^r1012021 and L3=(10)^r10120121 have adjacent distinct output symbols. Their stable last-to-first permutation equals f(i)=2^-1(i-1) mod p except the explicitly listed suffix splices; after y=i+1 the nonzero residue cycle is multiplication by 2^-1, with the old zero-coordinate fixed row incorporated by the suffix. Hence both full LF permutations have exactly one cycle, giving primitive-necklace inverse BWT images. Exact sorted-block agreement counts show d_H(L,F)=r+4=(p+3)/2 at both lengths, and the established lower bound U_k(n)>=ceil(n/2) gives sharp optimality for all eligible primes and ordered alphabets k>=3. Independently checked stable LF cycle length and exact Hamming distance for eight named primes and two lengths each. The splice argument, not the finite test, proves uniform p.
